key_insight: CORNETO’s ability to infer reliable biological networks varies across distinct robustness regimes. Its reusability depends on the available data, prior biological knowledge, regularization and biological context.
problem_solved: Determining when a previously developed multi-omics network inference framework can be reused reliably across different data and biological settings.
method: Study the reusability of CORNETO, a framework for learning biological networks from multi-omics data.
Assess how data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context relate to inference robustness.
Identify distinct regimes in which network inference is more or less robust.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the study highlights that reliable reuse requires evaluating data and domain assumptions—not just applying an existing framework. It motivates context-specific robustness checks before trusting inferred biological networks.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: multi-omics measurements and prior knowledge → CORNETO → inferred biological network.
Conceptual regime map showing robustness across data availability and prior-knowledge conditions.
Four-factor dashboard highlighting data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context.
Side-by-side network illustrations contrasting stable and sensitive inference outcomes.
paper_title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
paper_authors: Xabier Martínez-de-Morentin, Sumeer A. Khan, Itziar Cenzano, Robert Lehmann, Alberto Maillo
